Two prisoners named Chang Chi Ming A # ) 
and Ching Hao (¥ %&) alias Ching Chong Hwa 
(% 3 th )}, who were arrested in room 334, New 
World Hotel, 1 Bubbling Well Road, in connection with 
the distribution of handbills from the hotel onto Yu 
Ya Ching Road in the evening of March 11, 1939, were 
brought to Headquarters from Chengtu Road Station and 
subject to lengthy interrogation on March 13, 14 and 
16, 1939. Apart from admitting their respective parts 
in the distribution of the handbills, the two prisoners 
confessed that they are members of the“voe Shing Zoe 
(Rehabilitation Society) in whose name the handbills 
were issued. According to them, the Society has for 
its aim the rehabilitation of the area devastated as 
a result of the current hostilities. They also added 
that the principle promoters of the organization are 
two men named Chang and Dong and that the handbills 
were handed to them by the last named who has an 
office established at 495 Nerth Szechuen Road near 
Jukong Road. 

It is worthy of note that of the other eight 
prisoners who were taken into custody from room 334 
New World Hotel in the evening of March 11, 1939, and 
who were released the following day, March 12, 1939, 
one Chung Yung Nyi (# Ae ) (the 6th man arrested), 
Inspector of the Nanking Theatre, was stated by Chang 
Chi Ming to be also a member of the Voe Shing Zoe

independent organization, which aims at the rehabilitation of 
China and requested me to join. At this juncture my friend 


Koo Sung lauded the principles of the Society and urged me to

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

At 3.40 p.m. 24-7-39, I.P.I.s 107 & 30 1
and J.P.V.1107 brought to the Station the six
described accused whom they arrested at the
instigation of complainant Lee Song Foo (李双富)
on a charge of "Assault and Malicious Damage".

From complainant, his assistant and J.D.S.
3/4 it appears that complainant is a shop
keeper at No. 18 Ya Sing (楊新) Road, Shop at
No. 146 Police Road.

At 3 p.m. 24-7-39, the 1st accused went to
complainant's shop to buy 3 ice, two saka and
one bottle of mineral water & got a stamp but as
he had no change he asked for some Sai Nwing
Sien (山銀泉) mineral water. It was given. He
later started a quarrel with complainant
alleging that the ice was not very cold.

The 1st accused then went to Room No. 651 of the
Wing On (吳官) Hotel, 1 Po Foh Street, and
called out the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th accused
with several others unknown, all of whom returned
to complainant's shop at about 3.25 p.m. 24-7-39
and without making any conversation started a
fight with the complainant and two other assistants
named Sai Nwing Sien (山銀泉) and Tong Yau Yue
(湯堯色) using their fists. The 2nd accused
picked up a bottle of mineral water and struck
complainant over the head with it causing injuries.

The accused concerned together also caused
Malicious Damage by deliberately smashing one dozen
bottles of mineral water, and six water melons,

'Description of scalp, not serious'.

Questioned on detectives, the accused all admit the offence.

The 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th accused all act as touts for various girl guides bureau and they are of the lower class with no visible means of support and they sleep at night in the Woo Kung Hotel, Fokien Road.

The 6th accused is an associate of the others and was visiting them at the Hotel when he was called by the 1st accused to assist in the fight.

The accused have all been charged with "Assault" Jont. to Art. 277 of the J.J.J. and a further charge of "Malicious Damage" (See Louza F.I.R.2858/39) has been preferred against them.

They will be arraigned before the S.S.D. Court on 25-7-39.

Made by. D.S.I. Logan. Forwarded by. C. Crawford. S.I.

The two prisoners named Chang Chi Ming (張季明)
and Ching Hao (景豪) alias Ching Chong Hwa (景昌煥),
who were arrested in Room 334, New World Hotel, 1
Bubbling Well Road, on 11.3.39, were released by order
of the D.C. (Special Branch) from Chengtu Road Police
Station at 1.30 p.m., and 1.45 p.m., respectively, on
8.5.39.

After release, the first named was followed by
a Special Branch agent who observed that he boarded a
public ricsha and proceeded to a Cantonese food shop
at 310 Bubbling Well Road, from where he put through
a telephone call to one Tsai Ah Doo (蔡阿大) (Tel. No.
unknown) whom he asked to wait for him in front of the
Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road. Thereafter, he left the
food shop and walked to the Grand Hotel outside the
entrance of which he was joined by some five persons
whom he accompanied to Room 303. A watch is being
maintained on the occupants of Room 303 and efforts
are being made to ascertain their identity.

Upon being released, the second named was also
followed by a Special Branch agent. This man boarded a
public ricsha and also proceeded to 310 Bubbling Well
Road, from where he telephoned for a hired car. At
3.05 p.m., a Johnson hire car, Licence No.18579,
arrived in response to his telephone call, which he
entered and directed to drive west along Bubbling
Well Road. Enquiries revealed that he went to the

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. 9069 Date March 16, 1939）
Subject Distribution of handbills from the New World Hotel onto
Yu Ya Ching Road - interrogation of prisoners
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Crawford

Two prisoners named Chang Chi Ming (張季明)
and Ching Hao (景 豪) alias Ching Chong Hwa
(景昌煥), who were arrested in room 334, New
World Hotel, 1 Bubbling Well Road, in connection with
the distribution of handbills from the hotel onto Yu
Ya Ching Road in the evening of March 11, 1939, were
brought to Headquarters from Chengtu Road Station and
subject to lengthy interrogation on March 13, 14 and
16, 1939. Apart from admitting their respective parts
in the distribution of the handbills, the two prisoners
confessed that they are members of the Voe Shing Zoe
（批：attached a & a 9187）
(Rehabilitation Society) in whose name the handbills
were issued. According to them, the Society has for
its aim the rehabilitation of the area devastated as
a result of the current hostilities. They also added
that the principle promoters of the organization are
two men named Chang and Dong and that the handbills
were handed to them by the last named who has an
office established at 495 North Szechuen Road near
Jukong Road.

It is worthy of note that of the other eight
prisoners who were taken into custody from room 334
New World Hotel in the evening of March 11, 1939, and
who were released the following day, March 12, 1939,
one Chung Yung Nyi (龔永年) (the 6th man arrested),
Inspector of the Nanking Theatre, was stated by Chang
Chi Ming to be also a member of the Voe Shing Zoe

两名囚犯，名为张季明 (Chang Chi Ming)
和景豪 (Ching Hao)，别名景昌煥
(Ching Chong Hwa)，因涉及1939年3月11日晚
从酒店向爱多亚路分发传单一事，
于南京路 (Bubbling Well Road) 1号新世界酒店334房间被捕，
他们于1939年3月13日、14日和16日从成都路捕房
被带至总部，并接受了长时间的审讯。除了承认各自在分发传单中的作用外，

（批：附件 a & a 9187）
（复兴社）的成员，传单是以该社名义发行的。据他们称，
该社的宗旨是重建因当前战事而遭受破坏的地区。他们还补充说，
该组织的主要发起人是两名分别姓张和董的男子，
传单是由后者交给他们的，此人在靠近九江路的
四川北路495号设有办事处。

值得注意的是，在1939年3月11日晚从新世界酒店334房间

My name is Ching Hao, alias Ching Chong Hwan (景昌煥),
aged 23, native of Soochow, M/broker, residing together with
family at 6 Loh Yue Li (樂餘里), Kwangse Road.
When I was 14 years of age my parents (both now
deceased) brought me from Soochow to Shanghai. I joined the
Zu Tuh English School, Tsepoo Road, and after studying there
for one year, went to work in the Ching Loong Printing Press,
135 Tsepoo Road (now defunct) as an apprentice. On reaching
the age of 18, I, with capital given me by my parents,
started to operate a "Mei Fah" (美發) Printing Press at
28/160 Taku Road. At the end of August, 1937, I wound up
the affairs of my shop, then situated at 637 Avenue Edward
VII, owing to lack of business due to the Sino-Japanese
hostilities but continued to work in the same trade in the
capacity of a broker.
On or about 7/3/39, I met in the Yangtse Ball Room
Chang Chi Ming (張季明) and Koo Sung (顧森), two
friends of mine, whose acquaintance I made while frequenting
cabarets. They introduced to me a male Chinese named Dong
(章), aged about 35, speaking Shanghai dialect with a
Cantonese accent and wearing foreign style clothing. During
the meeting, Dong told me that one named Tsang (張) had
formed a "Voe Shing Zoe" (Rehabilitation Society), an
independent organization, which aims at the rehabilitation of
China and requested me to join. At this juncture my friend
Koo Sung lauded the principles of the Society and urged me to
participate in its activities. I agreed and gave Dong a

我叫景豪，又名景昌煥（景昌煥），
23岁，苏州人，职业为经纪人，与家人同住于广西路乐余里6号。
我14岁时，父母（现均已去世）将我從苏州带到上海。我进入乍浦路祖托英语学校就读，在那里学习一年后，到乍浦路135号（现已停业）的庆隆印刷所当学徒。年满18岁时，我用父母给我的资金，在大沽路28/160号开办了一家“美發”印刷所。1937年8月底，由于中日敌对行动导致生意清淡，我结束了当时位于爱多亚路637号的店铺事务，但继续以经纪人的身份从事同一行业。
1939年3月7日左右，我在扬子舞厅遇到了张季明（張季明）和顾森（顧森），这两位是我在经常光顾歌舞厅时结识的朋友。他们向我介绍了一位名叫董（章）的中国男子，约35岁，讲带有广东口音的上海话，穿着西式服装。会面期间，董告诉我，有一个叫曾（張）的人成立了一个“维新会”（Voe Shing Zoe，Rehabilitation Society），这是一个独立组织，旨在复兴中国，并邀请我加入。此时，我的朋友顾森赞扬了该会的宗旨，并敦促我参与其活动。我同意了，并向董提供了

In the afternoon of March 10, 1939, Chang and I met
Dong again in the Yangtse Ball Room when Dong told us that
he would assign us to do some propaganda work on March 11,
1939. After some discussions it was agreed that Chang and
I would engage a room in the New World Hotel on March 11,
1939, and throw from there pamphlets purporting to emanate
from the Voe Shing Zoe onto Yu Ya Ching Road. After the
dissemination of the pamphlets from the New World Hotel,
it was agreed that I would traverse streets in the business
centre in the Settlement and disseminate copies of the
pamphlet to pedestrians. In conclusion Dong ordered Chang
and me to obtain the pamphlets from him at Szechuen Road
Bridge (south end) at about 7 p.m. March 11, 1939.

At about 3 p.m. March 11, 1939, Chang and I met at
Sing Mei Mei Girl Guides Agency, 10 Foh Ziang Li, Foochow
Road, the proprietor of which is one named Wu Dah Hai
(吳大海), a friend of mine. Both of us then proceeded
to the New World Hotel, 1 Bubbling Well Road, on foot and
there booked room 334 for one day, at a rental of $4.50
per diem which was paid by Chang. After remaining in the
room for approximately 15 minutes, we left on the
understanding that we would meet at Szechuen Road Bridge
at about 6.45 p.m.

On leaving the hotel, I proceeded to the Yangtse Ball
Room and later to the Sing Mei Mei Girl Guides Agency,

1939年3月10日下午，我和张在扬子舞厅再次见到董，董告诉我们，他将指派我们在1939年3月11日做一些宣传工作。经过一番讨论，商定由我和张于1939年3月11日在新世界酒店开一个房间，并从那里向虞洽卿路抛撒声称出自“维新会”的宣传单。在新世界酒店散发传单后，商定我将穿越租界商业区的街道，向行人分发传单副本。最后，董命令我和张于1939年3月11日晚上7点左右在四川路桥（南端）从他那里领取传单。

1939年3月11日下午3点左右，我和张在福州路福祥里10号的新美美女子向导社见面，该社老板是我的朋友吴大海（吳大海）。随后我们步行前往南京路1号的新世界酒店，在那里以每天4.50美元的租金预订了334房间一天，费用由张支付。在房间里呆了大约15分钟后，我们离开，约定晚上6点45分左右在四川路桥见面。

离开酒店后，我前往扬子舞厅，后来又去了新美美女子向导社，

At about 6 p.m. I left the latter address and went to the Nanking Theatre, Avenue Edward VII, to see my friend Chung Yung Nyi (龔永年), Inspector of the Theatre, with a view to requesting him to come to play maj-jong with us in the Hotel. Chung agreed to my proposal and promised to come when he left the theatre after the last showing. On leaving the theatre, I went to Szechuen Road Bridge by a No.17th Route trolley bus arriving there at about 7 p.m. When I saw Chang Chi Ming waiting me in front of the Carlowitz Company with two newspaper parcels placed at his feet. He handed me one parcel which, I understood, contained the pamphlets for distribution and we both proceeded on foot to Nanking Road near Kiangse Road where we boarded a west bound bus for the New World Hotel, Bubbling Well Road.

At about 8 p.m. March 11, 1939, I threw a bundle of pamphlet from the balcony of the room in the New World Hotel onto Yu Ya Ching Road. By this time Chang had left the room and about five minutes later, I also left the hotel bringing 100 copies of the pamphlets in my pockets, which I had kept for distribution on the streets.

I proceeded on foot southward along Yu Ya Ching Road, and turned eastward into Foochow Road. Outside the Zao Shing Style Drama Theatre of the Great China Hotel, Foochow Road, I disposed of some 50 copies of the pamphlets and in the vicinity of Mei Yuan Restaurant, Foochow Road, I threw away the remaining 50 copies. 1939年3月11日晚上8点左右，我从新世界酒店房间的阳台向虞洽卿路抛撒了一捆传单。此时张已离开房间，大约五分钟后，我也离开了酒店，口袋里装着100份传单，准备在街道上分发。

My name is Chang Chi Ming (張季明), alias Zung Tseng
Foh (程真福), alias Zung Chih (程傑), alias Zung Ching Pao
(程金寶), age 32, native of Shanghai, residing in a house
in North Szechuen Road near Jukong Road, and employed with
the Central China Telephone Co., Darroch Road, Chapei.
At the age of seven my father (now deceased) who then
served as a cook in the home of M. Lesandre, the late
Chairman of the French Municipal Council, sent me to study in
the Tung Wei Primary School, Rue Brenier de Montmorand. At
the age of 13 I left the school and joined the Printing
Department of the French Municipal Council as an apprentice
and worked there until I was 23 (1930) when I was discharged
as a result of the retrenchment policy of the Council. I
was at that time residing at 31 Shing Yih Li, Route Zikawei,
with my wife.
In February, 1933, I went to Nanking and joined the
Electricity Company there as a worker, earning approximately
$1.00 a day. In 1936 I obtained a job as an electrician at
the Artillery School, Nanking, with a pay of $45.00 per
mensem.
At the beginning of June, 1937, all the artillery
units in the school were transferred to various places in
view of the tense situation then prevailing and the academy
was closed. At the end of June, 1937, I returned to Shanghai
and resided at 31 Shing Yih Li, Route Zikawei, together with
my son and daughter. My wife died while I was working in
Nanking.

我叫张季明（張季明），又名程真福（Zung Tseng Foh），又名程傑（Zung Chih），又名程金寶（Zung Ching Pao），32岁，上海人，居住在北四川路近菊康路的一所房屋内，受雇于闸北达罗克路华中电话公司。
七岁时，时任法公董局前主席莱桑德尔（M. Lesandre）先生家中厨师的父亲（现已去世）送我到勃伦尼尔·德·蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）的东威小学读书。13岁时我离校，进入法公董局印刷部当学徒，一直工作到23岁（1930年），因公董局实行裁员政策而被解雇。当时我与妻子住在徐家汇路信义里31号。
1933年2月，我前往南京，加入那里的电力公司当工人，每天收入约1.00美元。1936年，我在南京炮兵学校找到一份电工的工作，月薪45.00美元。
1937年6月初，鉴于当时的紧张局势，学校的所有炮兵部队被调往各地，学校关闭。1937年6月底，我回到上海，与儿子和女儿一起住在徐家汇路信义里31号。我在南京工作期间，妻子去世。

In September 1938, while the Sino-Japanese hostilities were in progress around Shanghai I, together with some 70 others joined the "Special Movement Corps" formed by the Chinese Military. The Corps was disbanded following the withdrawal of the Chinese troops from Shanghai in November 1937, whereupon I and some of my comrades retreated into the French Concession.

In December, 1937, I joined the Paris Furniture Co., 1268 Avenue Joffre, as a foreman worker. I was discharged owing to business depression in September, 1938, when I went to stay with a friend of mine named Koo Sung (顧森), who was formerly an employee of the Consolidated Tax Bureau, at No. 5 Kong Ning Tsung (康邨), Connaught Road. At the beginning of February, 1938, one Mr. Wong Tee Chih (王志傑), an employee of the Central China Electricity Co., 87 The Bund, whose acquaintance I made through Koo Sung obtained a job for me with the Central China Telephone Co., Darroch Road, Chapei.

A few days after I had started work in the company, Koo Sung asked me to call upon one Dong (童), at 495 North Szechuen Road, every morning before attending the company's office, to transmit messages between them, Koo having then no "pass" to go north of the Creek. It was at this time, that Koo told me that Dong was a section chief of the "Voe Shing Zoe" (Rehabilitation Society) whose object was to help the Chinese people to resume business and residence in the occupied area. According to Koo, the Chief of the

1938年9月，当中日敌对行动在上海周边进行时，我和其他约70人加入了由中国军队组建的“特种运动队”。随着1937年11月中国军队从上海撤退，该队解散，随后我和一些战友退入法租界。

1937年12月，我加入霞飞路1268号的巴黎家具公司，担任领班工人。由于业务萧条，我于1938年9月被解雇，当时我去投奔我的朋友顾森（顧森），他曾是统税局的雇员，住在康纳脱路康邨5号。1938年2月初，通过顾森认识的王志傑（Wong Tee Chih）先生，他是外滩87号华中电力公司的职员，帮我在闸北达罗克路的华中电话公司找到了一份工作。

我开始在公司工作几天后，顾森让我每天早上去上班前，去北四川路495号拜访一位姓董（童）的人，在他们之间传递消息，因为顾当时没有“通行证”去苏州河以北。就在那时，顾告诉我，董是“维新会”（Rehabilitation Society）的一个科长，该会的目标是帮助中国人民在被占领区恢复商业和居住。据顾说，该会的会长是

Society is one Chang ( 張 ), with offices in North Szechuen
Road and telephone numbers 41340 and 4252 (Chapei). (I don't
know whether these telephone numbers are correct, as I only
copied them down one day while in the Cha Loh Hotel). (Note
Telephone No. 41340 is registered in the name Nee Chong Chin
(          ), 114 Hanbury Road). Approximately ten days later,
Koo instructed me to stop calling on Mr. Dong because he
had obtained a "pass" which enabled him to go north of the
Creek himself. Mr. Dong is a native of Kwangtung, aged
about 35, and frequently visits the Great Eastern Tea Room
when he comes south of the Creek.

On or about 26/2/39, I removed from Koo's home then
situated at No. 33 Dah Shing Faung ( 大 兴 坊 ), Tatung Road,
to a house in North Szechuen Road near Jukong Road (my present
address) but continued to come south of the Creek after
working hours to meet my friends, chiefly Ching Hao ( 景 豪 )
alias Ching Chong Hwan ( 景 昌 煥 ), in the various cabarets,
including the Siao Yao Cabaret, Yu Ya Ching Road; Yangtse
Ball Room, Yunnan Road; Dah Loo Dance Hall, Ningpo Road; and
Cha Loh Cabaret, Yu Ya Ching Road. During these meetings
I came to know Chung Yung Nyi (  永 年 ) Inspector employed
in Nanking Theatre, and Tsu Kuh ( 朱 克 ) all of whom are
members of the Voe Shing Zoe (Rehabilitation Society).
Although they appeared to be discussing something during
every meeting I was barred from participating in the
discussions as I was ignorant and was only a very junior
member of the Society.

一位姓张（ 張 ）的人，办公室在北四川路，电话号码是41340和4252（闸北）。（我不知道这些电话号码是否正确，因为我只是有一天在查罗酒店抄录下来的）。（注：电话号码41340登记在尼忠钦（Nee Chong Chin）(          )名下，地址汉密尔顿路114号）。大约十天后，顾指示我不再去拜访董先生，因为他已经获得了“通行证”，可以自己去苏州河以北。董先生是广东人，约35岁，来到苏州河以南时经常去东亚茶室。

1939年2月26日左右，我从顾当时位于大同路大兴坊（ 大 兴 坊 ）33号的住所搬到了北四川路近菊康路的一所房子（我现在的地址），但下班后仍继续来到苏州河以南会见朋友，主要是景豪（ 景 豪 ），又名景昌煥（ 景 昌 煥 ），在各种歌舞厅，包括虞洽卿路的逍遥舞厅；云南路的扬子舞厅；宁波路的大陆舞厅；以及虞洽卿路的查罗舞厅。在这些聚会中，我认识了在南京大戏院任职的稽查龚永年（  永 年 ）和朱克（ 朱 克 ），他们都是“维新会”（Rehabilitation Society）的成员。虽然每次聚会他们似乎在讨论某些事情，但我被禁止参与讨论，因为我无知，且只是该会的一名非常低级的成员。

In the evening of March 10, 1939, while Ching hao
and I were in the Yangtee Ball Room, Mr. Doong came to join
us and told us that a quantity of propaganda in the form of
pamphlets were to be distributed on March 11, 1939. He also
instructed us to obtain the propaganda matter from him at
the Szechuen Road Bridge at 7 p.m. March 11, 1939. Dong
had mentioned this at a previous meeting in a room in the
Cha Loh Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, on March 7, 1939 when Chung
Yung Ayi, Tsu Kuh, Koo Sung, myself and several others
unknown to me were present. It was during this meeting that
we said farewell to Koo Sung who left Shanghai for Hongkong
on March 8, 1939 on a certain mission the nature of which I
don't know.

I and Ching Hao passed the night (March 10) in the
Sing Mei Mei Girl Guides Agency at 10 Foh Ziang Li, Foochow
Road, the owner of which is a friend of Ching.

At 3 p.m. March 11, 1939, Ching Hao and I went to the
New World Hotel, 1 Bubbling Well Road, and booked room 334
with the object of disseminating the pamphlets from the
room onto Bubbling Well Road. We stayed in the room for
about quarter of an hour and left on the understanding that
we would meet each other at Szechuen Road Bridge between
6 p.m. and 7 p.m.

On leaving the hotel I amused myself in the Sun Sun
Company and its roof garden until about 6.10 p.m. when I
proceeded to the Szechuen Road Bridge, arriving there at
about 6.30 p.m. I waited at the bus terminus in front of

1939年3月10日晚，当景浩（Ching hao）和我在扬子舞厅时，董先生（Mr. Doong）前来加入我们要告诉我们，一批以传单形式的宣传品将于1939年3月11日分发。他还指示我们于1939年3月11日下午7时在四川路桥从他那里领取宣传品。董曾在1939年3月7日于虞洽卿路查乐饭店（Cha Loh Hotel）的一个房间内举行的一次前次会议上提及此事，当时钟永义（Chung Yung Ayi）、朱古（Tsu Kuh）、顾松（Koo Sung）、我以及几名我不认识的人在场。正是在那次会议上，我们向顾松道别，他于1939年3月8日因某项任务离开上海前往香港，该任务的性质我并不知晓。

我和景浩在福州路福祥里10号的新美美女子向导社（Sing Mei Mei Girl Guides Agency）过夜（3月10日），该社老板是景的朋友。

1939年3月11日下午3时，景浩和我前往静安寺路1号新世界酒店，预订了334号房间，目的是从该房间向静安寺路散发传单。我们在房间里待了大约一刻钟后离开，约定在下午6时至7时之间在四川路桥会面。

离开酒店后，我在先施公司及其屋顶花园消遣，直到下午6点10分左右，随后前往四川路桥，于下午6点30分左右到达。我在

the Carlowitz Co. At about 6.45 p.m. Doong came in a Ford
Hire car from north of the Creek and after having handed me
a parcel of pamphlets together with $10.00 returned north
of the Creek. Prior to receiving the parcel from Doong,
I had ready in possession a parcel of oranges, which was
given to me by Ching Hao. A few minutes later, Ching
arrived on foot, and I gave him the parcel containing fruits.
We proceeded to Nanking Road near Kiangse Road where we
boarded a westbound bus for the New World Hotel. We
arrived at the New World Hotel shortly after 7 p.m. and
after remaining in our room for about twenty minutes, I
departed, leaving Ching in the room to distribute the
pamphlets. I left the room in order to evade my
responsibility, if anything unfavourable happened. Leaving
the hotel, I had a walk along Yu Ya Ching Road and in the
vicinity of the Great World Amusement Resort. About one
hour later, I returned to the hotel, whereupon I was
arrested.

With regard to the addresses found in my note book,
they were written by Koo Sung, abovementioned. The paper
which contains a brief account regarding amounts received
and spent was written by me, and it was merely a budget.
I hoped that I would receive a sum of $50.00 from Doong
after we distributed the pamphlets. The eight chops,
mentioned in this budget, were to be made on the instructions
of Doong, but he had not yet told me for what purpose
the chops were to be used.

Logan
16/3/31

麦边洋行（Carlowitz Co.）前的公交车终点站等候。下午6点45分左右，董乘坐一辆福特出租车从苏州河北岸过来，递给我一包传单以及10.00美元后，返回苏州河北岸。在从董那里接收包裹之前，我手中已持有一包橘子，这是景浩给我的。几分钟后，景步行到达，我将装有水果的包裹交给了他。我们前往靠近江西路的南京路，在那里搭乘了一辆向西行驶前往新世界酒店的公交车。我们在晚上7点后不久到达新世界酒店，在房间里停留了大约二十分钟后，我离开，留下景在房间里分发传单。我离开房间是为了万一发生不利情况以逃避责任。离开酒店后，我沿虞洽卿路及大世界游乐场附近散步。大约一小时后，我回到酒店，随即被捕。

关于在我笔记本中找到的地址，它们是由上述顾松书写的。那张简要记录收支金额的纸是我写的，那仅仅是一份预算。我希望在分发传单后能从董那里收到50.00美元。这份预算中提到的八枚印章，是按董的指示制作的，但他尚未告诉我这些印章将用于何种目的。

Logan
1939年3月16日

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Pro-Japanese Pamphlets Thrown from New World Hotel, 1 B'Well Road.
---------------------------

At 8.10 p.m. 11/3/39 a telephone message was received from Sinza Station reporting that pamphlets were being thrown from the New World Hotel, 1 B'Well Road.

C.D.J. 192 and the undersigned immediately attended and on arrival at the scene, learned from C.P.C. 3388 (Louza) that he had seen the pamphlets being thrown from a balcony on the 3rd floor of the New World Hotel facing Yu Ya Ching Road. Detectives searched 3rd floor rooms in this part of the hotel and on the balcony of Room 334 which was unoccupied at the time, found three pamphlets of the same kind as those distributed. Enquiry of the tea-boy, attending this room, Yao Ching Yue (姚慶餘) ascertained that the occupants, two male Chinese, had left the room shortly before arrival of detectives. Further enquiries disclosed that at 3 p.m. 11/3/39 a male Chinese wearing foreign clothes had engaged the room in the name of Chang Uhi Ming (張宇明) native of Pootung, Telephone Co. and then had gone out. At about 7.30 p.m. 11/3/39 this man returned with another male Chinese also wearing foreign dress and each carried a square shaped, newspaper wrapped

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Yao Ching Yue, 38, Married, residing No. 4 Chi
Zeu Li, off Connaught Road.
native of Ningpo taken by C.D.S. 192
at Ch. Rd. Stn. on the 11/3/39. and translated by Clerk Tan.

I am a teaboy (No. 54) employed by the New World Hotel,
No. 1 B'Well Road.

At 8 a.m. 11/3/39, I went on duty on the 3rd floor and
at 3 p.m. same date, a male Chinese wearing foreign dress,
(i.e. Chang Chi Ming, now in custody) appeared and stated
he wanted to open a room. I led him to Room No. 334 which
he engaged, gave me $5 rental in advance. He registered his
name as Chang Chi Ming, an employee of the Telephone Co.
Shortly after this, he left the hotel.

At about 7.30 p.m. I observed the above described person
accompanied by another male Chinese, also wearing foreign
dress, (i.e. Ching Chong Hwan, now in custody) enter the
booked room, each carrying under their left arm a paper parcel.
They both remained in the room until 8 p.m. when they left.

Shortly after their leaving the room, Police appeared and
from the balcony of Room No. 334 seized 3 copies of pamphlets.

At 9.30 p.m. the occupant again returned, this time he
was accompanied by a further stranger (i.e. Zah Ah Zoo, now
in custody).

Chengtu Road Station was informed and Police came and
took Tsang Chi Ming and his companion Zah Ah Zoo into custody.

At 10 p.m. Ching Chong Hwan, accompanied by an unknown
male Chinese (i.e. Zu Doo Shung, now in custody) and a Chinese
female (i.e. Tsang Zung Sz, now in custody) again came to the
room and were detained.

The Police attended the hotel and took them into custody.
I followed the Police to the station as a witness.
The above is my true statement.

Signed and crossmarked.

警方调查报告。

以下为姚庆岳（Yao Ching Yue），38岁，已婚，住康纳路（Connaught Road）支路芝微里4号，宁波籍人士之供词，由C.D.S. 192号警员于1939年3月11日在成都路捕房录取，并由谭书记员翻译。

我是受雇于北四川路1号新世界大酒店的茶房（编号54）。

1939年3月11日上午8时，我上三楼值班，同日下午3时，一名身穿西装的中国男子（即张季明 Chang Chi Ming，现已被拘押）出现，并称他要开一个房间。我带他到334号房间，他预订了该房间，并预付给我5元租金。他登记姓名为张季明，职业为电话公司职员。此后不久，他离开了酒店。

约晚上7时30分，我看见上述之人 accompanied by 另一名同样身穿西装的中国男子（即景昌焕 Ching Chong Hwan，现已被拘押）进入已预订的房间，每人左臂下夹着一个纸包。两人一直待在房间内，直到晚上8时离开。

他们离开房间后不久，警察出现，并从334号房间的阳台上查获了3份传单。

晚上9时30分，住客再次返回，这次他 accompanied by 另一名陌生人（即柴阿助 Zah Ah Zoo，现已被拘押）。

通知了成都路捕房，警察赶到并将张季明及其同伴柴阿助拘捕。

晚上10时，景昌焕 accompanied by 一名身份不明的中国男子（即朱道生 Zu Doo Shung，现已被拘押）和一名中国女子（即曾宗氏 Tsang Zung Sz，现已被拘押）再次来到房间，并被拘留。

警察前往酒店将他们拘捕。我作为证人跟随警察前往捕房。
以上是我的真实供词。

签名并画押。

The following is the rough translation of a letter
found in possession of the 6th named suspect Chung
Yoong Nyl (Vide Chengtu Road Misc. No. 100/39.)
------------------------------------------

Dear Mr. Yoong Nyien,

I understand you will leave here for
Chungking in due course and I hope you will enhance
gracefulness for our nation.

Being talented and capable, I am glad
to look forward that you will handle everything
at will.

Since your departure for that port is
in relation to the existence of China, you will
certainly not mind any matter of a trivial nature
and due to this, I forward to you herewith the sum
of $5.00 which you have invested in the Money Club
of which I am the promoter.

Yours Truly,

(Sd) Liang Ngoh Yuen.

October 8, 1939. Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

EAST ASIA PEACE MOVEMENT PROPAGANDA WEEK

The East Asia Peace Movement Propaganda Week will start to-day, October 8, and end on October 14. The object of this campaign is to enlighten the people about the present situation of the Chungking Government and the European War, to accelerate the establishment of a new central regime in China, to intensify the work for the construction of the new order in the Far East and to promote the spirit of rapprochement between China and Japan.

During this week, all residents within the occupied areas should hoist the Japanese flag and the five-barred flag and lanterns to celebrate the occasion.
Programmes for this week are listed as follows:-
October 8: (1) Ceremonial meeting.
(2) Lecture meeting.
(3) Propaganda work consisting of handbills, cartoons, etc.
(4) Exhibition of motion pictures.
(5) Dramatic plays.

REPORT
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
West Hongkew S. E. FOKASABY
December 31st 39.
Date: 2. S. D. 17-10-40
Subject. Erection by Japanese Naval Landing Party of a large cloth banner
at the rear of "E" Post, North Thibet-Kaifeng Roads.
Made by D.S. Bevan. Forwarded by [Signature] Inspector
Officer in charge

Sir,

At 3.40 p.m. 31-12-39 a telephone message was
received from the British Military "B" Sector, reporting
that the Japanese Naval Landing Party were erecting a
banner at the rear of "E" Post North Thibet-Kaifeng,
and requesting the services of a Japanese interpreter.

F.S.734(H) was summoned and accompanied by the
undersigned visited the scene.

On arrival it was seen that a large white cloth
banner had been hung across Kaifeng Road extension, about
five yards west of the Barricr Gate.

One end of the banner had broken free causing
it to furl in such a manner as to conceal the Chinese
characters printed on it. F.S.734 called a J.N.L.P.
sentry on duty in the vicinity and requested that we
be allowed to read it. However he refused the request
and removed the banner.

Enquiries revealed that the banner had been
hung at about 11 a.m. this instant by a Chinese under
the supervision of a member of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party.

Residents in the vicinity whilst being unable
to quote the characters gave a rough translation as
follows:-

The new order in Asia is for peace. Japanese
are not fighting the Chinese but fighting communism.

Lieutenant Marshall, i/c Seaforth Highlanders

事由：日本海军陆战队在西藏北路与开封路交界处“E”岗亭后方悬挂大幅布质标语。
撰写人：D.S. Bevan。呈报人：[签名] 督察
主管警官

先生，

1939年12月31日下午3时40分，接到英军“B”防区的电话消息，报告称日本海军陆战队正在西藏北路与开封路交界处的“E”岗亭后方悬挂标语，并请求派遣一名日语翻译。

警员 F.S.734(H) 奉召前往，由下文署名者陪同抵达现场。

到达后发现，一幅巨大的白色布质标语横跨悬挂在开封路延伸段上，位于路障闸门以西约五码处。

标语的一端松脱，导致其卷曲起来，从而遮盖了上面印有的汉字。警员 F.S.734 叫来附近执勤的一名日本海军陆战队哨兵，请求允许我们阅读标语内容。然而，他拒绝了这一请求，并将标语取下。

经查询得知，该标语是当天上午11时许，由一名中国人在一名日本海军陆战队成员的监督下悬挂的。

附近的居民虽然无法准确引用上面的汉字，但提供了大致如下的译文：

亚洲新秩序旨在和平。日本人并非在与中国人作战，而是在与共产主义作战。

马歇尔中尉，海福尔高地团负责人

Date April 10, 1939.

Subject. Anti-British, Anti-Communist and Anti-Kuomintang Propaganda
in Nantao.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien-pih Forwarded by Morgan 11/4

Under the auspices of the Japanese authorities,
an "Anti-British, Anti-Communist and Anti-Kuomintang
Propaganda Movement" was held in Nantao on April 9,
in the form of a procession. At 9 a.m., some 290
persons (consisting of 3 members of the Special
Service Department of the Japanese Military, 4 members
of the Nantao Administrative Office of the Shanghai
City Government, 10 members of the Anti-Communist
Youths' Group (防共青年團 ), 20 members of
the Nantao Police and 250 teachers and pupils of the
Dah Dao Primary School) gathered in the Dah Dao No.1
Primary School, 493 Chung Hwa Road, and proceeded in
processional order to the Nantao Bund, where they
boarded a Japanese vessel, the s.s. "Kiangsu Maru".
The vessel sailed on the Whangpoo until 11 a.m. when
the participants returned to have their tiffin.

At 2 p.m. all the participants re-gathered
and held a procession, traversing various roads in
and around the City. The procession terminated at
5 p.m. when the participants dispersed.

During the processions, those taking part
were equipped with banners bearing the following
inscriptions :-
1. Boycott British goods!
2. The first one who invaded China is Britain!
3. Retrocession of foreign settlements!
4. Establish the New Central Regime!

事由：南市地区的反英、反共及反国民党宣传。

撰写人：分区督察 范连璧 (Fan Lien-pih) 呈报人：摩根 4月11日

在日本当局的主持下，一场“反英、反共及反国民党宣传运动”于4月9日在南以游行形式举行。上午9时，约290人（包括3名日军特务机关成员、4名上海市政府南市办事处成员、10名防共青年团成员、20名南市警察以及250名大道第一小学的师生）在中华路493号大道第一小学集合，并按游行队列行进至南外滩，随后登上一艘名为“江苏丸”号的日本轮船。该船在黄浦江上航行至上午11时，参与者返回用午餐。

下午2时，所有参与者重新集合并举行游行， traversing 市内及周边各条道路。游行于下午5时结束，参与者随即解散。

在游行期间，参与者手持印有下列字样的标语：
1. 抵制英货！
2. 侵略中国之首恶乃英国！
3. 收回租界！
4. 建立新中央政权！

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 1 7 1939
“Scientific Basis Of ‘New Order In East Asia’”
Summary Of An Article In A Japanese Magazine; Class Consciousness Should Be Rejected By The Political Party Of Each State

The following is a summary of an article entitled “The Scientific Basis of the ‘New Order in East Asia’” which appeared in a recent issue of the Japanese magazine “Crisis,” a publication of some merit and standing amid a section of the Japanese intelligentsia. It is based on the opinions and theories of such authorities as Mr. T. Kawai, spokesman of the Gaimusho; Dr. Royama, one-time professor at the Tokyo Imperial University; and, particularly, Mr. M. Yamazaki, an economist.

The human race, especially the European race, now faces the greatest problem ever to confront it. It is whether warfare can cease forever or not. Indeed it stands on the parting of the ways of permanent peace or human slaughtering. In East Asia, Japan has brought out of the dark shadow of warfare a thesis for establishing permanent peace in the Orient which may be extended to the whole world. It is the theory of the “Co-operative Body of East Asia.” Why does the Body serve to maintain peace in East Asia? In order to clarify the theory it will be necessary to refer to the evolution of warfare.

The earliest warfare was between tribes. With the development of society, warfare was waged in a more large scale between peoples, and then between nations. At this last stage, warfare was often waged by a dominant class in a nation for the pursuit of its private interests, as was witnessed in past wars in Europe. Now that the art of war has been marvellously developed owing to the progress of science, any modern war entails the mobilization of the wealth, materials and human power of a whole nation.

It cannot, therefore, be waged merely for the consideration of the interests of a particular class. This is accounted for by the fact that the number of wars has been much reduced, but at the same time its scale has been extended so much that almost all nations in Europe take side of the two belligerent parties. This was exemplified in the world war of 1914-18.

The next world war which is threatened in Europe has an origin in the maintenance of the status quo by democracies and the breaking of the same by the totalitarian states which are “have-not nations.”

“Went Too Far”

In East Asia, the race-consciousness of the Chinese nation culminated in the revolutions of 1926-7, and succeeded in uniting the nation, and establishing a modern independent state, formally at least, but the revolutionary movement went too far by trying to drive the Japanese influence from Manchuria.

Then Japan retaliated, as she knew too well that by being driven away from the Asiatic continent Japan could hardly assure her existence, and that with China and Japan separated, China herself could not hope to maintain even her own independence. Japan realized on the basis of the experience of the World War that the only means of safeguarding her existence and effecting development consisted of forming an enlarged economic unit by the adjacent states and races.

It should, however, be borne in mind that this theory of the “New Order of East Asia” was not ex-pressed until the Sino-Japanese hostilities had progressed far, although the idea had long been entertained by the Japanese nation in the more crude form of “Asia for Asiatics.”

It is the result of the recognition of the fact that the Asiatic races can be expected to attain their object of liberation by effecting a stronger unity, respecting one another’s racial traditions and prestige. Because of this, Japan showed great sympathy towards the Kuomintang revolution, and some revolutionists, including Sun Yat-sen, took sanctuary in the private homes of some Japanese leaders as political refugees when their revolt against the Chinese Imperialistic regime failed.

As it is, when these Chinese revolutionary leaders attained power they began to refuse collaboration with Japan for the realization of “Asia for Asiatics” by treating her as a similarly aggressive Imperialistic nation to those in Europe, and they even wanted to drive her influence out of the Asiatic continent.

Kuomintang Recalcitrant

This recalcitrant attitude on the part of the Kuomintang culminated in the Manchurian Incident which has subsequently been developed into the China Incident.

In the course of the hostilities, Japanese aspirations put on a theory-formula which is the “Co-operative Body of East Asia” or a “New Order of East Asia.” The theory itself is by no means new, but it is expounded in a new formula based on a historical background.

Authorities who introduced the theory-formula are Dr. D. M. Royama, a former Professor of Tokyo Imperial University, Mr. M. Yamazaki, a prominent economist; Mr. T. Kawai, spokesman of the Foreign Office in Tokyo; and a few others.

Dr. Royama says: “The evolution of Japanese-Manchoukuo relations has traced a line which was quite unexpected by magnates of Japanese capitalism, for often it turned against their personal advantages. Why? Because defensive economics and at the same time geographically linked economics accompany a plan for economic development and as such can be distinguished from the Imperialism of Western Europe which has for its basic power pure capitalism. In short, it is not colonial economics, but a league of nations in a specified sphere where they share the same need of opposing external invasion. This ideology has been made clearer with the breaking out of the Sino-Japanese war. The Manchurian and the China Incidents cannot be explained by the commonplace colonial or commercial imperial-

1939年4月17日
“‘东亚新秩序’的科学基础”
一篇日本杂志文章的摘要；各国政党应摒弃阶级意识

以下是对近期日本杂志《危机》（Crisis）上发表的一篇题为“‘东亚新秩序’的科学基础”的文章摘要，该刊物在日本部分知识分子中具有一定的价值和地位。文章基于外务省发言人 T. Kawai 先生、前东京帝国大学教授 Royama 博士，特别是经济学家 M. Yamazaki 先生等权威人士的观点和理论。

人类，尤其是欧洲种族，正面临着前所未有的最大问题。即战争能否永远停止。确实，人类正处于永久和平与相互屠杀的分岔路口。在东亚，日本从战争的阴影中提出了一种在东方建立永久和平的理论，该理论可扩展至全世界。这就是“东亚协作体”理论。为何该协作体能维持东亚和平？为了阐明这一理论，有必要回顾战争的演变。

最早的战争是部落之间的战争。随着社会的发展，战争在更大规模的人民之间展开，随后是在国家之间展开。在最后这个阶段，战争往往由一个国家内的统治阶级为了追求其私人利益而发动，正如过去欧洲的战争所见。如今，由于科学的进步，战争艺术得到了惊人发展，任何现代战争都意味着动员整个国家的财富、物资和人力。

因此，战争不能仅仅出于考虑特定阶级的利益而发动。这解释了为什么战争的数量大大减少，但同时其规模扩大到了几乎欧洲所有国家都站在两个交战方中的一方。1914-18年的世界大战便是例证。

欧洲面临的下一场世界大战，其根源在于民主国家维持现状与作为“无产国家”的极权主义国家打破现状之间的冲突。

“做得过火”

在东亚，中华民族的种族意识在1926-27年的革命中达到顶峰，成功统一了国家，并至少在形式上建立了一个现代的独立国家，但革命运动试图将日本势力驱逐出满洲，此举做得过火。

随后日本进行了反击，因为她深知，如果被赶出亚洲大陆，日本很难确保其生存；而且如果中日分离，中国自身也无法希望维持其独立。日本基于世界大战的经验认识到，保障其生存和实现发展的唯一手段是与邻近国家和种族组成一个扩大的经济单元。

然而，必须牢记，“东亚新秩序”这一理论直到中日敌对行动深入发展后才被明确提出，尽管日本国民长期以来以更粗糙的“亚洲人治亚洲”形式怀有这一想法。

这是基于这样一种认识的结果：即亚洲种族通过加强团结，尊重彼此的种族传统和威望，有望实现其解放目标。正因如此，日本对国民党革命表示了极大的同情，当一些革命者反对中国帝制政权的起义失败时，包括孙中山在内的一些革命者曾作为政治难民避难于一些日本领导人的私宅中。

事实上，当这些中国革命领导人掌权后，他们开始拒绝与日本合作以实现“亚洲人治亚洲”，而是将日本视为与欧洲类似的侵略性帝国主义国家，甚至想将其势力赶出亚洲大陆。

国民党顽固不化

国民党这种顽固态度导致了满洲事变，随后发展为卢沟桥事变（中国事变）。

在敌对行动过程中，日本的愿望形成了一种理论公式，即“东亚协作体”或“东亚新秩序”。这一理论本身绝非新颖，而是基于历史背景以新的公式加以阐述。

引入这一理论公式的权威人士包括：前东京帝国大学教授 D. M. Royama 博士、著名经济学家 M. Yamazaki 先生、东京外务省发言人 T. Kawai 先生以及其他几人。

Royama 博士说：“日满关系的演变轨迹完全出乎日本资本主义巨头们的意料，因为它常常违背他们的个人利益。为什么？因为防御性经济以及地理上 linked 的经济伴随着经济发展计划，因此可以与以纯粹资本主义为基本力量的西欧帝国主义区分开来。简而言之，它不是殖民经济，而是在特定领域内的国家联盟，它们有着共同抵御外部入侵的需求。随着中日战争的爆发，这一意识形态变得更加清晰。满洲事变和中国事变不能用普通的殖民或商业帝国主义来解释——

组成一个在物质上和意识形态上共同抵御外敌入侵的国家联盟，必然拥有共同的意识形态和共同的文化。如果支持泛美主义的各共和国没有共同的文化，没有共同的民主政治学说——简言之，没有共同的意识形态立场，那么泛美主义将完全失去其内在意义。

更进一步
山崎（Yamazaki）先生在阐述新理论时更进一步，因为他视东亚新秩序为世界新秩序的萌芽。据他看来，满洲事变及其后续的中国事变，构成了新世界危机以及随之而来的世界新秩序建立的最重要因素。
“如何形成东亚种族的合作体？”他问道。“它不能通过让人想起自由主义政治论题的旧式国家间条约来结合或解散，也不能像外交谅解那样，由组成该实体的成员国出于方便而联合或分裂。
“东亚种族之间实际合作关系的形成，将采取具有历史意义的联合宣言的形式；当然，该宣言必须假定组成该实体的各民族和国家的意志是通过清晰的理论和原则协调并统一的。宣言必须表达该实体的历史意义，以及基于新世界观念的社会学说；它必须是一份关于通过东亚的政治和社会解放而发生的世界革命的明确宣言，并且是执行该宣言的意志、体系和方法的体现。
“该宣言在本质上必须完全不同于那种其中缔约国所表达的意志与各民族的生活没有直接关系的宣言。它不仅规范国家之间的关系，而且通过一种新学说规范缔约方大众的生活，并由各国的共同法律所支持。”

“最高目标”
“这一宣言本身必须是东亚种族政治生活的最高目标，规范联邦的政治、经济和文化使命，并阐释其基本理论。”
山崎先生驳斥了日本想在中国建立“傀儡政府”的说法，他说：
“东亚种族的新关系并不预设在没有理论或原则支持的情况下，将一个民族的意志强加于其他种族。如果在这种情况下，上述联合宣言是由一个所谓‘傀儡政府’发布的，而该政府在其国内缺乏基础，那么它就不可能成为产生新秩序的推动力。
“联合宣言必须在各国之间建立精神纽带。简言之，每个参与国都必须由一个基于国民生计并得到大众支持的民族政党来统治。每个政党必须有一种共同的道德冲动，以促**〔此处转录不清〕**

"By the collaboration of such racial and national political parties of the states forming the Co-operative Body of East Asia a unified co-operative organ connecting the States must be formed, regulating the administration of each State by a fixed formula. And all the nations must unite themselves horizontally through various organs of their social life so as to form a human tie closely connecting the nations. As regards the political party of each state, it must partake of racial and national character; it must reject any class consciousness."
In organizing an ideal national political party, Mr. Yamazaki does not expect much from any wealthy or privileged class which feels no incompatibility between its daily life and the evolution of the social structure. The party will, on the other hand, find great supporters in the middle class, intelligentsia, labourers, peasants who want to be liberated from the bondage of the present social structure.
Such a party supported by the masses, however, must not be a political system which is inclined to class warfare for the special interests of the members of the party. Those who join the party must have a strong social conscience, and a strong sensitiveness to justice. They only join the party not as representatives of the social stratum to which they belong, but as the leaders of the national life as a whole.
As regards the economic relations between the co-operative body of East Asia and the rest of the world, Mr. Yamazaki says that such relationship will never be severed, but since the economics of the body must be one which is freed from liberalistic capitalism its relationships with the economics of the outside world will have to be adjusted by political considerations. For example, trade based on mutual reciprocity or compensation will be preferred to one of laissez faire economics.
This does not mean to separate East Asia from the rest of the world, but it is in conformity with the requirement that East Asia shall be given a status of independence, and not the semi-colonial dependence of the Western capitalism, and with that status alone it is expected to co-operate with the other parts of the world.

Mr. Kawai's Theory
Mr. Kawai in his work "The Goal of Japanese Expansion" refers to the economic aspect of the new order of East Asia with the following remarks:—
"At the present stage of human progress, no country can fully satisfy its multifarious needs by the resources to be found within its own boundaries, but it must inevitably seek to expand its sphere of cultural and economic activity. Japan, Manchoukuo and China, fully appreciating the world significance of the motto, 'Three nations, one in virtue,' and their relationship of mutuality, should co-operate for their common prosperity under the Asiatic system so as to make their countries a powerful link in the future chain of world economy."
Needless to say the new order in East Asia means the dawn of new era of permanent peace in this part of the world, for the new order secures the East Asiatic continent against any foreign invasion by extending and intensifying the area of defence. With the increase of world population, and progress of society, warfare has been geographically extended from conflicts between tribes to **〔此处转录不清〕**

“通过组成东亚合作体的各国种族性和民族性政党的协作，必须形成一个连接各国的统一合作机构，并通过固定的公式规范各国的行政。所有国家必须通过其社会生活的各种机构横向联合起来，从而形成紧密连接各国的人类纽带。至于各国的政党，它必须具备种族和民族特征；它必须拒绝任何阶级意识。”
在组织理想的民族政党时，山崎先生不指望那些日常生活与社会结构演变之间感觉不到任何不兼容的富裕或特权阶级给予太多支持。另一方面，该党将在中产阶级、知识分子、劳工和农民中找到巨大的支持者，这些人希望从当前社会结构的束缚中解放出来。
然而，这种得到大众支持的政党，绝不能是一个倾向于为党员特殊利益进行阶级斗争的政治体制。加入该党的人必须具有强烈的社会责任感和对正义的强烈敏感度。他们加入该党并非作为其所归属的社会阶层的代表，而是作为整个民族生活的领导者。
关于东亚合作体与世界其他地区的经济关系，山崎先生说，这种关系永远不会断绝，但由于该实体的经济必须是摆脱自由主义资本主义的经济，其与外部世界经济的关系将不得不通过政治考量进行调整。例如，基于相互互惠或补偿的贸易将优于自由放任的经济贸易。
这并不意味着将东亚与世界其他地区隔离开来，而是符合赋予东亚独立地位的要求，而不是西方资本主义下的半殖民地依附地位，并且只有凭借这种地位，才期望与世界其他地区合作。

河合（Kawai）先生的理论
河合先生在其著作《日本扩张的目标》中，通过以下言论提及东亚新秩序的经济方面：—
“在人类进步的现阶段，没有任何国家能够完全依靠其境内资源满足其多种多样的需求，但它必然寻求扩大其文化和经济活动的范围。日本、满洲国和中国充分领会‘三国一德’这一口号的世界意义及其相互关系，应在亚洲体系下为共同繁荣而合作，从而使各国成为未来世界经济链条中的有力一环。”
不用说，东亚新秩序意味着世界这一地区永久和平新时代的黎明，因为新秩序通过扩展和加强防御区域，保护东亚大陆免受任何外来入侵。随着世界人口的增长和社会的进步，战争在地理上已从部落间的冲突扩展到**〔此处转录不清〕**

on Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek
and urged support of the puppet
“Reformed Government.” At the
same time, they accused the British
of helping the Chinese National
Government and urged a boycott of
British goods.
Shortly after dawn yesterday
morning, similar leaflets were
found in the department store area
off Nanking Road. These were
discovered on Kir Wo Ka, the
narrow thoroughfare which runs
alongside the Wing On Company
and extends back from Nanking
Road. These pamphlets were of
the same type found on Robison
Road.
Some connection is seen between
the leaflets found in Shanghai
yesterday and the anti-British
campaign recently inaugurated in
Nanking, Hangchow, and Kaifeng.
This campaign, according to re-
ports received here, was started
with a parade at Kaifeng
and as a result of the leaflets
found in Shanghai, it is believed
that the propaganda mongers have
finally extended their activities to
this city.

Britain, Soviet Attacked

On March 31, in Nanking, at a
meeting of the “Joint Commission”
of the puppet Nanking and Peiping
regimes, Great Britain and the
Soviet Union were attacked as
“Bandits of egoism, fishing in
troubled waters,” and “Devils go-
ing about under the mask of
peace.”
The incentive for this outburst
on the part of the puppet rulers
was the alleged backing given to
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek by
these two Powers. The “Joint
Commission” expressed determin-
ation to support Japan in her
fight against the “menace of com-
munism” and for the establish-
ment of a **〔此处转录不清〕** in East
Asia.

1939年4月7日

反英
运动在此
展开

谴责蒋介石
和英国的传单
张贴在墙上

傀儡政权
攻击列强

在南京会议上
英国、苏联被称为
“强盗”、“魔鬼”

上海公共租界警务处的侦探昨晚仍在试图确定昨天清晨在西区墙壁和房屋上发现的大量反中国国民政府和反英宣传传单的来源。这些传单是由在罗宾森路（Robison Road）和斐伦路（Ferry Road）沿线巡逻的中国巡捕发现的。他们随后将这些传单全部移除，并将副本送至工部局警务处总部进行翻译。
后来得知，这些传单包含对蒋介石委员长的猛烈攻击，并敦促支持傀儡“维新政府”。同时，它们指责英国帮助中国国民政府，并呼吁抵制英货。
昨天清晨天亮后不久，在南京路附近的百货公司区域也发现了类似的传单。这些传单是在吉沃卡（Kir Wo Ka，音译）发现的，这是一条狭窄的街道，沿着永安公司（Wing On Company）一侧延伸，从南京路向后延伸。这些传单与在罗宾森路上发现的类型相同。
人们认为，昨天在上海发现的传单与最近在南京、杭州和开封发起的反英运动之间存在某种联系。根据此处收到的报告，这场运动始于开封的一次游行，鉴于在上海发现的传单，人们相信宣传煽动者最终已将活动扩展至本市。

英国、苏联遭到攻击

3月31日，在南京举行的傀儡南京和北平政权“联合委员会”会议上，英国和苏联被攻击为“趁火打劫的利己主义强盗”和“披着和平面具招摇过市的魔鬼”。
傀儡统治者爆发此次抨击的动机，据称是这两个强国向蒋介石委员长提供了支持。“联合委员会”表达了支持日本对抗“共产主义威胁”并为在东亚建立**〔此处转录不清〕**的决心。

These declarations of the puppet
regimes, although they were cabled
to Japan and "Manchukuo" by the

published in Dairen.
"General Chiang Kai-shek and
his party, both civil and military,
usurped the government of the
country and pursued their own
interests," the puppets resolved. "In
alliance with communists, the
public enemy of mankind, they in-
flamed Japan, our friendly
neighbor, to conflict, and dared to
throw the country and people into

"Notwithstanding all this, Bri-

out to realize their malevolent de-
sires, at the sacrifice of Far

the current hostilities," stated
the declaration.

傀儡政权的这些声明，虽然通过同盟通信社（Domei）的附属机构国策通讯社（Kokutsu Agency）电告日本和“满洲国”，但并未发送至世界其他地区。会议的完整报告是随着4月1日版的《满洲日报》（The Manchuria Daily News，在大连出版的英文日报）抵达上海时才收到的。
“蒋介石将军及其文武党派篡夺了国家政府并谋取私利，”傀儡政权决议称。“他们与人类的公敌共产党人结盟，煽动我们的友好邻邦日本陷入冲突，并胆敢将国家和人民推入毁灭的深渊。
“尽管如此，英国和苏联通过向蒋介石将军提供援助，企图牺牲远东人民并延长当前的敌对行动，以实现其恶意欲望，”声明称。

Pamphlets

“Agitation” In S’hai

Demonstration

Bitterly attacking the Chinese
National Government and strongly
denouncing Great Britain’s policy
in China, some pamphlets were
found pasted up on the walls and
dwelling houses in the badlands
facing Robison Road.
More pamphlets, berating the
Chinese leader, Generalissimo
Chiang Kai-shek, were discovered
in Kin Wo Ka, the narrow street
which runs alongside the Wing
On Company.
Pro-Japanese
The posters which were stuck up
on Robison Road were located in
the stretch of road between
Penang Road and Jessfield Road,
while the pamphlets found in the
downtown area were lying on the
street, near Kiukiang Road.
It is believed that the posting
and distribution of these anti-
National Government and anti-
British leaflets were done by per-
sons who had been paid by pro-
Japanese factions.
Kaifeng Parade
Some connection is seen between
the pasting of the pamphlets de-
nouncing British policy and the
campaign which has recently been
inaugurated by the pro-Japanese
Chinese “governments” to stir up
anti-British feeling among the
masses of the Chinese people.
This campaign was introduced
with an anti-British demonstra-
tion and parade in Kaifeng and
now it appears that these pro-
paganda mongers are spreading
their literature in the Shanghai
area, even in the Settlement it-
self.

1939年4月6日

坏地带简报
攻击英国
在墙上发现

罗宾森路传单
抨击蒋介石

在吉沃卡（Kin Wo Ka）
发现传单

上海“煽动”
继开封示威之后

一些传单被发现张贴在面向罗宾森路的贫民区（badlands）的墙壁和住宅上，猛烈攻击中国国民政府并强烈谴责英国在华政策。
更多辱骂中国领袖蒋介石委员长的传单在吉沃卡（Kin Wo Ka，音译）被发现，这是沿着永安公司一侧的一条狭窄街道。
亲日
张贴在罗宾森路上的海报位于槟榔路（Penang Road）和极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）之间的路段，而在市中心区域发现的传单则散落在九江路（Kiukiang Road）附近的街道上。
人们认为，张贴和分发这些反国民政府和反英传单的是受亲日派系雇佣的人员。
开封游行
人们认为，张贴谴责英国政策的传单与亲日中国“政府”最近发起的在中国民众中煽动反英情绪的运动之间存在某种联系。这场运动以开封的一次反英示威和游行为开端，现在看来，这些宣传煽动者正在上海地区，甚至包括租界本身，散布他们的宣传品。

（批：Lier 2/4）

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated April 6 and other local newspapers :-

Anti-British Posters

Large numbers of coloured handbills
were posted yesterday morning at the entrances of the
branches and sub-stations of the Police Bureau of the
Shanghai City Government at Zau Ka Tu, Jessfield Road,
Robison Road, Penang Road and other places in the
Western District.

According to information, the handbills
contain the following anti-British slogans in support of
the anti-British movement advocated by the Japanese
sponsored "Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic"
"Don't forget that the first country
which invaded China is Great Britain!"
"Chiang Kai-shek, the Communist Party
and Great Britain are three-in-one devils harmful to
mankind!"
"Let us establish a new Central
Government without delay!"
"Recover the Foreign Settlements and
abolish consular jurisdiction!"
A brief study of the contents of these
handbills will convince one that they constitute an
attempt on the part of the Japanese and the puppet
authorities to instigate the Chinese people to engage in
an anti-British movement. It is said that these handbills
were posted at various places by the Japanese and the
puppet authorities yesterday, but they were destroyed
secretly by the Chinese people. For this reason and as
a means of protection, fresh posters were affixed in
front of the various branches of the Police Bureau.

（右侧手写批注：Sp Bi / Enquiry）
（右侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE / 7 APR. 1939）

4月6日的《大美晚报》及其他本地报纸：-

反英海报

昨天上午，在曹家渡（Zau Ka Tu）、极司菲尔路、罗宾森路、槟榔路（Penang Road）及西区其他地方的上海市政府警察局各分局和分所入口处，张贴了大量彩色传单。

据消息人士称，这些传单包含以下支持日本扶持的“中华民国维新政府”所倡导的反英运动的反英标语：
“不要忘记第一个侵略中国的国家是英国！”
“蒋介石、共产党和英国是危害人类的三位一体魔鬼！”
“让我们立即建立一个新的中央政府！”
“收回外国租界并废除领事裁判权！”
简要研究这些传单的内容即可使人确信，这是日本人和傀儡当局企图煽动中国人参与反英运动。据说这些传单日由日本人和傀儡当局在各处张贴，但被中国人秘密销毁。因此，作为一种保护手段，新的海报被张贴在各个警察局分局门前。

（右侧手写批注：Sp Bi / 查询）
（右侧印章：上海工部局 / 总监办公室 / 1939年4月7日）

（底部手写批注：J.C.S.B. / 附件归档。/ JBP / 助理秘书致副总监（特别处）/ 10/4）

CHINA PRESS.
MAR 1 6 1939
0210
9069
30 3 39

Japan Said Driving
Toward Full Control
Of China’s Economy

Hankow C.O.C. Leader
Gives Report At
Annual Meet

“No amount of moral indignation
—no amount of idle talk of the
‘New Order in East Asia’—can dis-
guise the stark fact that Japan is
relentlessly consolidating her ap-
proach to her real objective—the
creation of a military and economic
bloc in East Asia under her sole
dominance.

“Aided by the succession of major
crises which have threatened to
convulse Europe, Japan has seized
with both hands the opportunity of
pursuing her expansionist designs
in China, undeterred by almost
universal condemnation and un-
restrained by international pres-
sure.”

This was the frank and unminc-
ing statement made by Mr. W.
Bowling, chairman of the Hankow
British Chamber of Commerce, at
the annual general meeting held in
the Wuhan city on March 7.

“A free currency and freedom of
trade with equality of rights and
opportunity,” he said, “form the
only basis on which any future in
China can be viewed with confi-
dence.”

Foreigners Cut Out

“Whether or not the Japanese
objective can be consummated by
the methods she is at present em-
ploying is open to question,” he
continued, “but it is meanwhile an
essential part of her program that
all third party influences and
interests (nor does this exclude her
partners in the Anti-Comintern
Pact) must be ruthlessly and uni-
laterally eliminated.”

A partial report of Mr. Bowling’s
speech follows:

“So far as Wuhan is concerned
the strangling process has been
completed practically in one stage,
by the severance of rail connection
with the seaboard, and the closure
of the river.

“We have the satisfaction of
knowing that by refusing to eva-
cuate, we have preserved at least
a good proportion of our material
property and rights from usurpa-
tion, but so long as we remain cut
off from communication with the
outside world, what we have saved
savors of Dead Sea fruit.

Must Realise Crisis

“Do not think me unduly pessi-
mistic. I am not. But it is essen-
tial that we should realise the full
magnitude of the crisis in which
**〔此处转录不清〕**
the future of those interests may
well be determined within the next
few months.

“The year under review falls into
two sharply demarcated sections
which I will describe as the ante
and post-occupation periods. The
first period saw China immersed in
military operations on a scale and
of an intensity her rulers can
scarcely have visualised.

（批：File）
（批：Cie）
（批：Rups 14/3）

《字林西报》。
1939年3月16日
0210
9069
39年3月30日

据称日本正推动
全面控制
中国经济

汉口英国商会主席
在年度会议上
发表报告

“无论多少道德义愤
——无论多少关于‘东亚新秩序’的空谈——都无法掩盖一个严峻的事实，即日本正在无情地巩固其迈向真正目标的手段——在其独家主导下在东亚建立一个军事和经济集团。

“在欧洲面临一系列可能引发动荡的重大危机的帮助下，日本双手抓住了在中国追求其扩张主义计划的机会，几乎不受普遍谴责的影响，也不受国际压力的约束。”

这是3月7日在武汉举行的年度大会上，汉口英国商会主席 W. Bowling 先生所作的坦率且毫不含糊的声明。

他说：“自由的货币和贸易自由，以及平等的权利和机会，构成了任何人对中国未来抱有信心的唯一基础。”

排除外国人

“日本能否通过其目前采用的方法实现其目标，尚存疑问，”他继续说道，“但与此同时，其计划的一个重要部分是必须无情且单方面地消除所有第三方影响和利益（这并不排除其在《反共产国际协定》中的伙伴）。”

以下是 Bowling 先生演讲的部分报告：

“就武汉而言，窒息过程实际上在一个阶段就完成了，即切断了与沿海地区的铁路连接，并封闭了河道。

“我们欣慰地知道，通过拒绝撤离，我们至少保全了相当一部分物质财产和权利免受篡夺，但只要我们就仍与外界隔绝沟通，我们所保存的东西就如同死海果实一般（意指看似美好实则无用或有害）。

必须认识到危机

“不要认为我过于悲观。我并不悲观。但我们必须充分认识到危机的全部规模，其中 **〔此处转录不清〕**
这些利益的未来很可能在未来几个月内决定。

“回顾的一年分为两个界限分明的部分，我将之描述为占领前和占领后时期。第一个时期见证了中国陷入其统治者几乎无法想象的规模和强度的军事行动中。

（批：归档）
（批：Cie）
（批：Rups 14/3）

pages.en:
"With the issue still in the
balance on wide fronts, we also saw
behind the lines the spectacle, also
perhaps scarcely visualized, of a
China truly united behind her
leaders. The Government had its
quarters here right up to the last
moment, and many of us can vouch
from personal contact and observa-
tion that the new spirit knitting
the Chinese nation together in its
adversity was no chimera of the
propagandist, but something very
real and vital.
Spirit Lives
"Will mere military reverses kill
that spirit? The lessons of history
point otherwise.
"For an example of the new spirit
which animated a China in arms,
I cannot do better than recall the
magnificent and successful effort to
maintain external communications
via the Hankow-Canton Railway.
"This railway was aptly described
as China's life-line, and we may be
forgiven for taking a particular
pride in its amazing performance,
since the Hankow British played so
large a part in the inception of the
scheme.
Asks Co-operation
"I think it is fair to say that we
have acceded with a good grace to
such restrictions as the Japanese
forces have deemed it necessary to
impose, but it would make for
better feeling and understanding if
there were evidence of a little more
give and take.
"It will be remembered that
within a fortnight of the closure
of the River in August 1937 initial
shipments were made by rail to
Hongkong and from then onward
this route received the full attention
of the National Government.
"At first it proved to be a very
halting route and timely relief was
given to shippers by the short-lived
Tungchow Canal route during the
autumn of that year. From Feb-
ruary onward a great improvement
in the Railway route became ap-
parent, an improvement which
reached its maximum in May and
then gradually fell away under the
stress of military necessity and
enemy attack.
"It enabled the Exporter to carry
on a fair portion of his trade, for
the most part on remunerative
terms.
"It is estimated that by this route
some 60,000 tons of export cargo,
other than cotton and minerals,
went forward, this figure including
35,000 tons Woodoil, 6,000 tons
Chinagrass, Tea, egg products, hides
and skins, gallnuts, bristles and
sundries.
"In certain commodities, particu-
larly egg products (other than
frozen), and Chinagrass, there was
actually no decrease in the ordinary
European and American trade.
Trade Hazardous
"The conduct of this trade was
difficult and hazardous. Actual
shipment, which had usually to be
made at the shortest notice, was
often fraught with danger to those
supervising it consequent upon air-
raids and the resulting dislocation.
The transit of goods was subject
to unpredictable delay and constant
risk of destruction. More serious in
the actual result was loss through
"petty" pilferage and damage to
cargo due to exposure.
pages.zh:
“鉴于战局在广阔战线上仍呈胶着状态，我们也目睹了后方一种或许鲜为人知的景象：一个真正团结在其领袖身后的中国。政府直至最后一刻仍将其总部设于此地，我们许多人可以凭亲身接触和观察作证，那种在逆境中将中华民族凝聚在一起的新精神，并非宣传家的海市蜃楼，而是某种非常真实且充满活力的存在。

精神长存

“单纯的军事挫折会扼杀这种精神吗？历史的教训指向相反的答案。

“若要举例说明这种赋予武装中国以生命的新精神，我最好不过地回顾一下经由汉口-广州铁路维持对外通讯联络的那项宏伟而成功的努力。

“这条铁路被恰如其分地描述为中国的生命线，鉴于英国汉口方面在该计划的发起中发挥了如此巨大的作用，我们为其惊人的表现感到特别的自豪，这也是情有可原的。

呼吁合作

“我认为可以公允地说，对于日军认为有必要施加的限制，我们已欣然予以接受；但是，如果能表现出更多的相互妥协，将有助于增进良好的感情和理解。

“人们会记得，在1937年8月黄浦江航道关闭后的两周内，首批货物即通过铁路运往香港，此后，这条路线得到了国民政府的充分重视。

“起初，事实证明这是一条非常不稳定的路线，那年秋天，短暂开通的通州运河路线及时为发货人提供了救济。从2月起，铁路运输路线有了显著改善，这种改善在5月达到顶峰，随后在军事必要和敌人攻击的压力下逐渐衰退。

“它使出口商能够继续开展相当一部分贸易，且大多是在有利可图的条件下进行的。

“据估计，通过这条路线运出的出口货物（棉花和矿产品除外）约有6万吨，这一数字包括3.5万吨桐油、6000吨苎麻、茶叶、蛋制品、皮革和毛皮、五倍子、鬃毛及杂项物品。

“在某些商品方面，特别是蛋制品（冷冻品除外）和苎麻，传统的欧美贸易实际上并未减少。

贸易风险重重

“开展此类贸易既困难又危险。实际装运通常必须在极短的通知期内完成，由于空袭及其造成的混乱，负责监督装运的人员往往面临危险。货物的运输遭受不可预测的延误，并时刻面临被毁的风险。更为严重的实际后果是因‘零星’盗窃和货物暴露受损而造成的损失。

pages.en:
"But the greatest hazard of all
was that of falling markets for the
length and uncertainty of transit—
to say nothing of the interval inter-
vening between application for and
receipt of shipping facilities—were
such that it became virtually im-
possible to dispose of cargo prior
to its arrival at Hongkong.
"The allocation of space was
placed in the hands of the Joint
Transportation Bureau, which was
virtually a department of the For-
eign Trade Commission. That por-
tion of it, which was not reserved
for Government requirements, was
allocated fairly and without dis-
crimination.
"The partial but not ineffective
Exchange restrictions which were in
force at the time of our last Annual
Meeting, were replaced in April by
a system of Exchange control, under
which all Exchange against export
goods had to be sold directly or
indirectly to the Government Banks
who strictly maintained the official
Bill rate of 1/2% and 29%.
"The stability of Exchange, albeit
at a level 75% higher than that
of the open market, on the whole
assisted the trade.
Stability Given
"There were doubtless cases of
individual hardship, arising from
the difficulty of competing with dis-
tricts where the open rate prevail-
ed, but it cannot be doubted that
the general stability which it im-
parted, served the general conduct
of trade in that it eliminated spe-
culation and inflation at this end
and wild fluctuations and uncon-
trollable markets abroad.
"On the purely financial side.
Exporters, though they did not like
the interruption in their normal
arrangements and relations, suffered
no actual hardship, the Bank of
China having been fully ready to
grant all necessary and reasonable
facilities.
"The usual problems, of which
the normal life of the exporter is
composed, particularly crops and
market conditions abroad, played
but an unimportant role in the ex-
ceptional conditions prevailing.
"Of crops very little is known, but
on the whole weather conditions
were unfavorable, and it may be
assumed that that feature and the
general dislocation arising out of
the political situation combined to
make them below the normal.
Prices Low
"Prices for most, though by no
means for all commodities, were
held fairly steadily at a rather low
level. Trade was not curtailed by
lack of cargo, but on the other
hand there were very few indica-
tions of supplies weighing on the
market either here or upcountry.
"Most of what was available
eventually found buyers. There
was neither a rush to sell nor any
deliberate effort to withhold cargo.
High transportation costs must in
most cases have made prices unre-
munerative to the original seller
and, as usually happens in such
cases, quantities marketed were
much below the normal.
"My report naturally covers that
period which ended about the
middle of October. The remainder
of the year was of course a period
of complete stagnation, and stag-
nation which unfortunately persists
and shows no signs of lightening."
pages.zh:
“但最大的风险莫过于市场下跌，因为运输路程漫长且不确定——更不用说在申请和获得航运设施之间 intervening 的时间间隔——使得在货物抵达香港之前 virtually 不可能处理掉货物。

“舱位分配由联合运输局负责，该局实际上是对外贸易委员会的一个部门。其中未保留给政府需求的部分，得到了公平且无歧视的分配。

“在我们上次年度会议时生效的部分但并非无效的外汇限制，于4月被一套外汇管制体系所取代。根据该体系，所有针对出口货物的外汇必须直接或间接出售给政府银行，这些银行严格执行1/2%和29%的官方汇票汇率。（注：此处原文数据可能指特定汇率机制或贴水率，依原文译出）

“尽管汇率水平比公开市场高出75%，但其稳定性总体上促进了贸易。

给予稳定

“毫无疑问，由于难以与盛行公开汇率的地区竞争，出现了个别困难的情况，但不可否认的是，它所带来的总体稳定性服务于贸易的总体运作，因为它消除了这边的投机和通货膨胀，以及国外市场的剧烈波动和不可控局面。

“仅从纯金融角度来看。出口商虽然不喜欢其正常安排和关系的中断，但并未遭受实际的困难，因为中国银行已完全准备好提供所有必要和合理的便利。

“构成出口商正常生活的常见问题，特别是农作物收成和国外市场状况，在 prevailing 的特殊情况下只扮演了微不足道的角色。

“关于农作物收成知之甚少，但总体而言天气条件不利，可以推测，这一因素以及政治局势引起的普遍混乱相结合，导致收成低于正常水平。

价格低迷

“大多数商品（虽非全部）的价格相当稳定地保持在较低水平。贸易并未因缺乏货物而缩减，但另一方面，无论是本地还是内地，市场上供应积压的迹象都很少。

“大部分可用货物最终都找到了买家。既没有抛售潮，也没有故意扣留货物的行为。在大多数情况下，高昂的运输成本必然使价格对原始卖家来说无利可图，而且，正如这类情况通常发生的那样，上市数量远低于正常水平。

“我的报告自然涵盖了截至10月中旬左右的时期。这一年余下的时间当然是完全停滞的时期，而这种不幸的停滞持续至今，且毫无缓解迹象。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
MAR 24 1938

New Order in Asia:
A Malayan Chinese View

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—The Japanese are seeking a "New Order in Asia-ism", but in essence what does this mean?

Press and propaganda, both by the Japanese themselves and pro-Japanese organs, have sung paeans of the efforts attendant on this "order" and there is no doubt that a certain section of people, (both Chinese and foreigners), have been misled into seeing the genuineness of the Japanese viewpoints. Minds that are be-fogged, misguided or prejudiced fall in the latter category but thinking people cannot be blind for long to the series of outrageous acts perpetrated to bring about this "new order."

Are bombing of open towns calculated to win over or to awe the hearts of the peasant Chinese? And yet Japan believe that the more towns bombed, the sooner will the response to the "new order" be. Apart from questions of humanitarian considerations, this is only to underrate the will of the Chinese people to resist.

For whoso devotes a little thinking to the tactics and aims of the invaders will soon awake to the realities of the situation which is bared as under:—

(1) Bombing of open towns which is deprecated by any righteous individual is used as part of the Japanese routine programme of conquest.

(2) Their technique of winning over the immobile rabble on the occupation of a city is often to offer the latter drugs and flesh, so that by glutting the primitive human desires the people may become insensate to their moral obligations.

(3) Using the puppet states as a mouthpiece whenever they want to vent their anger or disapproval of the foreign Powers' actions in China.

(4) Propaganda and threats to the people living within the occupied areas, so as to make them amenable to Japanese control. (A good instance is the recent promulgation of the Peking Provisional Government that a month or two hence no Chinese National Currency notes would be allowed for circulation in the Northern occupied territory under pain of a very heavy penalty).

(5) Seizure of Chinese properties located in occupied areas and the many illegal money-making projects under way in order to justify military expenditures and adventures in China.

(6) Listen to this:—
"According to the measure of their control over the various districts which have been occupied by their troops, the Japanese have monopolized China's produce, firstly to provide the needs of their army in the field, secondly to supply essential raw materials for Japanese industry, both in China and at home, and thirdly so that the foreign currency value of the remainder, which is available for export to Europe and America, should whenever possible pass into the hands of Japanese-controlled banks."

(7) Must the "new order" also include the sacking and burning of Chinese educational institutions, to make way for the "culture" of the invaders?

(8) Noticeable also is the superiority complex of Japanese youths towards Chinese nationals in China, which can only be inferred as a natural consequence of the stationing of Japanese troops in China. Would such an attitude be conducive to the avowed aims of Nippon?

《字林西报》，1938年3月24日

亚洲新秩序：
一位马来亚华人的观点

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——日本人正在寻求一种“亚洲新秩序主义”，但这本质上意味着什么？

无论是日本人自己还是亲日机构的新闻和宣传，都对伴随这一“秩序”的努力大唱赞歌，毫无疑问，某些人群（包括中国人和外国人）已被误导，看到了日本观点的“真实性”。头脑糊涂、被误导或抱有偏见的人属于后一类，但善于思考的人不会长期对为实现这一“新秩序”而犯下的一系列暴行视而不见。

轰炸不设防城镇是为了赢得还是震慑中国农民的心？然而，日本相信，轰炸的城镇越多，对“新秩序”的响应就会越快。除了人道主义考虑的问题外，这只能说是低估了中国人民抵抗的意志。

任何稍加思考入侵者战术和目标的人，很快就会清醒地认识到如下赤裸裸的现实：—

(1) 轰炸任何正直人士都谴责的不设防城镇，被用作日本常规征服计划的一部分。

(2) 他们在占领城市时收买不动民众的技术，往往是向后者提供毒品和肉欲，以便通过满足原始的人类欲望，使人们对道德义务变得麻木不仁。

(3) 每当他们想要发泄愤怒或对列强在华行动表示不满时，就利用傀儡国家作为传声筒。

(4) 对生活在占领区内的人民进行宣传和威胁，使他们顺从日本的控制。（一个很好的例子是最近北平临时政府颁布的规定：一两个月后，除非受到严厉惩罚，否则不允许中国国币在北方占领区流通）。

(5) 没收位于占领区的中国财产，并进行许多非法牟利项目，以证明其在华的军事开支和冒险行为是正当的。

(6) 请听这一点：—
“根据其对军队占领的各个地区的控制程度，日本垄断了中国的物产，首先是为了满足其野战部队的需求，其次是为日本国内及在华工业提供必要的原材料，第三是为了使剩余可供出口到欧洲和美洲的部分的外汇价值，尽可能流入日本控制的银行手中。”

(7) “新秩序”是否也必须包括洗劫和焚烧中国教育机构，以便为入侵者的“文化”让路？

(8) 同样值得注意的是，日本青年对在华侨民表现出优越感，这只能推断为日军驻扎在中国的必然结果。这种态度有利于日本所宣称的目标吗？

如果我们所见和正在见证的一切并不意味着为了暗示一种“亚洲新秩序主义”而征服中国，那么任何一个神志正常的人都很难挑出这个荒谬短语的含义！

我们不久前听到关于吴佩孚元帅的消息是什么？说他愿意领导开封的“治安维持委员会”，条件是“日本从中国撤军”。众所周知，这一提议已被间歇性地搁置，鉴于日本对这位不愿成为日本棋子的元帅施加的压力，这一点也不奇怪。他们再次提出这个问题：“当日本人说他们在中国没有领土野心时，他们是真的真诚吗？”如果不是，那么从日本官员口中掉出的那些陈词滥调就只是一堆胡言乱语。

“亚洲新秩序主义”只能意味着一件事——那就是日本的统治和对中国的实际控制，以便岛国帝国可以在政治、经济、社会和文化领域随心所欲地对待中国人及其国家。

一位马来亚华人。
上海，3月24日。

CHINA PRESS.
MAR 1 8 1939
02950

TO the Indians of Shanghai,"
is the caption of a leaflet
now being circulated among the
Sikh and other Indian residents
of this city.
"Indians in Shanghai, open
your eyes to the important truth
that lies behind the current
Sino-Japanese conflict," declares
the first paragraph of the leaflet.
From this point on, the
message tells the Indian living
in this city that the wise thing
for him to do is to recognise
Japan's plans for a "new order"
in East Asia.

The leaflet, devoted entirely to a
tirade against the British and the
Chinese National Government, is
the first of its kind to appear here;
the first sign that pro-Japanese
propagandists have started the work
of spreading their "new order" chit-
chat among the Sikhs.

Written in excellent English, the
leaflet is also evidence that persons
back of this bit of propagandizing
have engaged individuals of some
intelligence to do their scribbling.
Where the propagandists slipped
up, however, is in printing the
leaflet in English. Only a com-
paratively small percentage of the
Indians living in Shanghai are able
readers of the English language.

Much of the message contained on
the leaflet is a back-biting attack on
the International Settlement. In
this connection, it states that the
"Settlement is not only a shame
morally, but it is also a defeat for
Asia from the political point of
view." In conclusion, the leaflet,
which is signed by an individual
calling himself Bhagat Singh, "Sec-
retary of the Young Asia League,"
calls upon all Indians in this city
to be prepared to shoulder their
"share in the abolition of the Inter-
national Settlement."

A copy of the leaflet which fell
into our hands was one of several
hundred distributed by a Chinese
along Bubbling Well and Nanking
Roads last week. The man carried
the leaflets in a large sack, strapped
on his shoulders. He confined their
distribution to Indian watchmen
employed by the shops in these dis-
tricts, carefully avoided Indian
constables and traffic officers.

Satisfactory solution of the
shoot-up of two Japanese junior
members of the army publicity
office and their two girls friends,
which occurred just outside the
Kwan Sun Yuen Restaurant on
Nanking Road on Chinese New
Year's Day is still lacking.

One of the Japanese was
slightly wounded, but he was
not examined by any foreign
doctor south of Soochow Creek,
and whatever was known of his
condition was learned from Japan-
ese police reports.

27/3.

1939年3月18日
02950

“致上海的印度人，”
这是一份目前正在本市
锡克教徒及其他印度居民
中传单的标题。
传单第一段宣称：“在上海的印度人，
睁开你们的眼睛，看清当前
中日冲突背后的重要真相。”
从这一点开始，
该文告告诉居住在本市的印度人，
明智之举是承认日本在东亚建立
“新秩序”的计划。

这份传单通篇都是对英国和
中国国民政府的猛烈抨击，是此类
在此地出现的第一份；这是亲日
宣传家开始在锡克教徒中散布其
“新秩序”论调的第一个迹象。

该传单英文写得很好，这也证明
幕后策划者雇佣了一些有才智的人
来撰写这些文字。然而，宣传家
失策之处在于用英文印刷传单。
居住在上海的印度人中，只有相对
较小比例的人能阅读英文。

传单中的许多内容是对公共租界的
恶意攻击。在这方面，它声称
“租界不仅在道德上是一种耻辱，
而且从政治观点来看也是亚洲的失败。”
最后，这份由自称“青年亚洲联盟”
“秘书”的巴格特·辛格（Bhagat Singh）
署名的传单，呼吁本市所有印度人
准备好承担他们“废除公共租界”的
“那份责任”。

落入我们手中的一份传单，是上周
一名中国人在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）
和南京路一带分发的数百份中的一份。
此人将传单装在一个大袋子里，背在肩上。
他只向这些地区商店雇用的印度巡捕分发，
刻意避开了印度警员和交通警。

农历新年当天，在南京路冠生园
（Kwan Sun Yuen Restaurant）餐馆外发生的
两名日本陆军报道部初级成员及其两名
女友遭枪击事件，至今仍未得到圆满解决。

其中一名日本人受轻伤，但他未接受
苏州河以南任何外籍医生的检查，
关于其伤情的任何了解均来自日本
警方的报告。

27/3.

It appears that the gunman
fired at the four of them,
huddled together in a stationary
motorcar, from point-blank
range, but failed to wound any-
one seriously.

* * *

It will be recalled that, because of
the somewhat remote connection of
the two men with the Japanese
Army, quite an incident was develop-
ed of the affair, with the Nipponese
indignantly labelling it a political
terrorist act of a definite anti-
Japanese nature.
The hullabaloo came just at the
time when the Japanese were press-
ing demands on the Shanghai
Municipal Council, and they put
their finger on this particular in-
cident to drive home their point.

* * *

Quite a quantity of lard is at
present being exported from the
International Settlement to Europe
and America. This lard, however,
is not rated as first quality abroad,
because the still primitive Chinese
methods of manufacture have re-
mained practically unchanged for
centuries.
The Council's Public Health De-
partment, at present supervising all
such factories and plants, is now
working on a plan whereby lard
from Shanghai should rank with
the best.
There is no reason why, with the
introduction of modern methods,
lard from China should not take
its place along with the best in the
world's markets.

* * *

Things are happening so
rapidly in the Settlement that
the S.M.P. headquarters on
Foochow Road is buzzing with
activity, and departmental heads
are in a whirl. Some of them,
even on Wednesday, did not
know that the Japanese Special
Naval Landing Party had for-
mulated additional traffic re-
gulations for Settlement districts
north of Soochow Creek. Yes-
terday, many officials were com-
pletely ignorant of the fact that
the regulations were already in
force.

* * *

The additional regulations, in-
cidentally, do an injustice to famed
Japanese thoroughness. They pro-
vide against smoking while driving
a motor vehicle, but have overlooked
what is vulgarly referred to as
"necking," as well as nose-picking.

看来枪手是从极近的距离
向挤在一辆静止汽车里的四人
开枪，但未造成任何人重伤。

* * *

值得回顾的是，由于这两人与
日本军队有着某种较为疏远的联系，
此事演变成了一起相当严重的事件，
日本人愤怒地将其定性为具有明确
反日性质的政治恐怖行为。
这场喧嚣恰好发生在日本人向
上海公共租界工部局施压提出要求
之时，他们抓住这一特定事件
来强化他们的立场。

* * *

目前，大量猪油正从公共租界
出口到欧洲和美洲。然而，这种猪油
在国外并不被视为一等品，因为
仍然原始的中国制造方法几个世纪
以来几乎未变。
工部局公共卫生处目前监管所有
此类工厂和作坊，正在制定一项计划，
以使上海猪油跻身最佳品质之列。
随着现代方法的引入，中国猪油
完全有理由在世界市场上与最佳产品
并驾齐驱。

* * *

租界内事态发展如此迅速，以致
福州路的工部局警务处总部忙碌不堪，
各部门主管忙得团团转。有些人
甚至在星期三还不知道日本特别
海军陆战队已为苏州河以北的租界
地区制定了额外的交通规则。昨天，
许多官员完全不知道这些规定
已经生效。

* * *

顺便提一下，这些额外规定
对著名的日本式细致入微是一种不公。
它们禁止在驾驶机动车时吸烟，但却
忽略了俗称的“搂抱亲热”（necking），
以及挖鼻孔的行为。

SECRET

March 13, 1939.

THE NEW ORDER OF ASIA - FROM THE KUOMINTANG VIEWPOINT.

The so-called "New Order of Asia" may be
described as a revolutionary movement aiming at the abrogation
of the "Status Quo" in this part of the world. Ever since
the Sino-Japanese war forty-five years ago, the United States
of America with a view to insuring her right for economic
expansion in the Far East, strongly advocated the policy of
open door and equal opportunity, which aimed at frustrating
Japan's ambitions and plans. Subsequently, under the auspices
of the United States Government and with the same purpose in view
the Nine Power Treaty and the Kellogg Pact were concluded by
the powers interested in the Far East. The peace of the
Far East was thus preserved through balance of power among the
nations concerned; the Far East having become the common market
for America, Great Britain, France, Japan and other powers and
none of these nations was able to monopolize the trade to any
great disadvantage of the others. Needless to say, this
situation was most dissatisfactory to Japan who has long
cherished the desire of domination. But owing to the fact
that she was not strong enough to challenge the Status Quo,
she was obliged to wait for a suitable opportunity. It happened
that during the years about 1929, the United States and also
Great Britain were badly stricken by an unprecedent economic
upheaval and they were forced by circumstances to concentrate
their main efforts on internal problems. Having seized this
opportunity, the Japanese started their aggressive program by
creating the Mukden Incident on September 18, 1931. This
venture was successful as the various powers were unable to
agree on a united action due to differences existing among them.
Japan found the situation most favourable and she continued to
push her aggressive campaign in China. After the Mukden
Incident, she occupied the whole of Manchuria and part of North

1939年3月13日。

亚洲新秩序——从国民党视角看。

所谓的“亚洲新秩序”可以描述为一场旨在废除
世界这一地区“现状”的革命运动。自从
四十五年前的中日战争以来，美利坚合众国
为了确保其在远东的经济扩张权利，大力倡导
门户开放和机会均等政策，其目的是挫败
日本的野心和计划。随后，在美国政府的主持下，
出于同样的目的，各有关列强签订了
《九国公约》和《凯洛格公约》。远东的
和平 thus 通过相关国家之间的力量平衡得以维持；
远东已成为美国、英国、法国、日本和其他列强的
共同市场，没有任何一个国家能够垄断贸易而
使其他国家处于极大不利地位。不用说，这种
局面令长期怀有统治欲望的日本极为不满。但由于
其实力不足以挑战现状，
她不得不等待合适的时机。恰逢
1929年左右，美国和英国
遭受了前所未有的经济动荡的重创，被迫
将主要精力集中在内部问题上。日本抓住这一
机会，于1931年9月18日制造了沈阳事变（即九一八事变），
开始了其侵略计划。由于各国之间存在分歧，
无法就联合行动达成一致，这次冒险取得了成功。
日本发现局势对其极为有利，便继续
在中国推进其侵略活动。沈阳事变后，
她占领了整个满洲和华北部分地区

（左侧手写批注：Des B. / 3/12 / D.C. (特别科) / 归档 / 712）

China, which encroachments eventually lead to the present
war between China and Japan. Now, Japan, assuming the role
of conqueror, begins her program of permanent domination
by attempting to overthrow the status quo created by the
United States and other powers in the past. This attempt on
the part of Japan is being met with protests and opposition
from all powers concerned, who now realize their mistakes in
the past in having allowed Japan a free hand. On the other
hand, Japan, now openly declares that she is the stabilizing

made by Prince Konoye on November 3rd and November 18, 1938,
and the main points of his statements were as follows:-
(1) That all powers should recognize Japan as the
leading power in Asia.
(2) That all Asiatic questions should be solved by
the Asiatics themselves and that no interference from such
powers as the United States, Great Britain, France and Soviet
Russia shall be tolerated.
(3) That any scheme for the cultural or financial
development sponsored by the above mentioned powers must
be carried out with the co-operation of Japan.
(4) That the principal forces in Asia are Japan,
China and Manchukuo and that only with the co-operation of
these three nations can the new order in Asia be established.
(5) That for the above reason, Japan, China and

reconstruction of Asia.
(6) That the National Government of China under the

must be overthrown and replaced by a new regime willing to

中国，这些侵蚀最终导致了当前的
中日战争。现在，日本以征服者的姿态，
试图推翻过去由美国和其他列强建立的
现状，开始其永久统治的计划。日本的
这一企图正遭到所有相关列强的抗议和反对，
它们现在意识到过去允许日本自行其是
是错误的。另一方面，日本现在公开宣称
她是远东的稳定力量，因此，决心不顾
其他列强的意见，执行其既定政策。关于
这一问题最著名的声明是由近卫亲王于
1938年11月3日和11月18日作出的，其
声明要点如下：
(1) 所有列强应承认日本为
亚洲的领导力量。
(2) 所有亚洲问题应由
亚洲人自己解决，不容许美国、英国、法国和
苏维埃俄国等列强进行干涉。
(3) 由上述列强赞助的任何文化或金融
发展计划，必须在日本的合作下进行。
(4) 亚洲的主要力量是日本、
中国和满洲国，只有在这三个国家的合作下，
才能建立亚洲的新秩序。
(5) 基于上述原因，日本、中国和
满洲国应结成一个集团，在亚洲的经济、文化、军事和政治
重建方面密切合作。
(6) 由于蒋介石将军领导下的中国
国民政府无法领会日本的善意，并在列强的
煽动下坚持门户开放和机会均等政策，
必须予以推翻，并由一个愿意

pages.en:
- 3 -

co-operate with Japan in the creation of a new order in Asia.
To speak plainly and briefly, the so-called new
order of Asia aims at the elimination of all foreign interests
in the Far East and the making of Japan the supreme power
in this part of the world.. The new order week which has been
launched by Japanese organizations in Shanghai serves to
propagate these objects among their own nationals as well as
among local Chinese. The agitation against the International
Settlement recently waged by the local Japanese authorities
is suspected to be part of Japan's program in the new order
movement.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

与日本合作创建亚洲新秩序的新政权取而代之。
简而言之，所谓的亚洲新秩序
旨在消除远东的所有外国利益，并使日本
成为世界这一地区的最高权力。由在上海的
日本组织发起的“新秩序周”活动，旨在
向其本国国民及当地中国人宣传这些目标。
当地日本当局最近发动的针对公共租界的
煽动活动，被怀疑是日本在新秩序
运动中计划的一部分。

Date ____ / ____ / ____

13th March, 1933.

Y . Miura, Esq.,
H.I.J.M. Consul-General,
Shanghai.

Sir,

It has been brought to the attention of the
Council that facing Jessfield Road there have been posted
on the walls of the premises of the Western District
Branch Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government
No. 92 Jessfield Road, posters bearing the following
slogans:

"Take back the Foreign Concessions."
"Abolish Extraterritoriality."
"Down with the Foreign Powers which have
refused China to a semi-colony."

In view of the close connection that is known
to exist between the Japanese Gendarmerie and this Police
Bureau, I hope that you will agree with me that it is
desirable that posters of this nature should not appear.
At the present time efforts are being made at your request
for the establishment of closer cooperation between the
Japanese Gendarmerie and the Police of the International
Settlement, and a spirit of cooperation will not be
assisted if the Japanese Gendarmerie countenance attacks
upon the Settlement in this manner.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient Servant,

(Sgd) C. Holl S. Franklin

Chairman.

EB.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 15 MAR. 1933）

鉴于已知日本宪兵队与该警察分局

Made by. D.I. Pan Lien-pih, Forwarded by C Crawford
On March 8, copies of an anti-Foreign
handbill, purporting to emanate from the "Shanghai
City Government," were distributed by Chinese
policemen in Chapei and Kiangwan. Apart from
denouncing General Chiang Kai-shek and advocating
the enforcement of the so-called "New Order Movement",
this document accuses the Foreign Powers of having been
instrumental in China's civil wars in the past and
of having oppressed the Oriental people by economic
means. A copy of the handbill is attached together
with summarized translation.
Pan Lien-pih
